audit_findings.title: Positive-growth cases require a reversal of documented contraction
audit_findings.magnitude: Base versus bear adds $1,012m of equity value ($8.27/share); bull versus bear adds $1,428m ($11.66/share)
audit_findings.mechanism: The assumed 3% and 5% OE growth rates increase forecast OE and terminal value, which supplies 49.7% and 50.9% of those cases.
audit_findings.evidence: During the three fiscal years ended December 27, 2025, our net sales declined at a compounded annual rate of 1.9% reflecting the contraction of the U.S. home products market and a decline in demand in our international markets, partially offset by an increase in sales resulting from acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The historical contraction is demonstrated: 2023-2025 sales CAGR was negative 1.9%, and first-half 2026 sales declined another 3.2%, including market softness, service problems and share losses. Whether those pressures are permanent remains unresolved, but the computed $8.27-$11.66 per-share sensitivity is large enough to materially affect intrinsic value, even though all reported scenarios remain below the $43.11 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain organic volume, China sales, market-share and normalized-margin evidence by segment; then rerun the base and bull cases using only growth and terminal assumptions supported by that evidence.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may be a restructuring trough rather than run-rate OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $89.6m of FY2025 pre-tax headquarters charges, equal to 35.3% of the $253.9m OE anchor, including $71.6m cash and $18.0m non-cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash restructuring costs can depress anchor OE, while non-cash charges may already be reversed in the OE calculation; an unjustified add-back of recurring transformation costs would inflate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the fifty-two weeks ended December 27, 2025, we incurred total charges of $ 89.6 million, including cash charges of $ 71.6 million primarily related to severance and other exit costs, and non-cash charges of $ 18.0 million primarily related to acceleration of property, plant and equipment depreciation.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges and their scale are demonstrated, but an anchor error is not: the record does not reconcile which amounts entered the $253.9m OE calculation or establish their recurring cash burden. The uncertainty is material because the disclosed charge is more than one-third of the anchor. Continued headquarters costs in 2026 and the increased $100m-$120m aggregate estimate also caution against treating the entire amount as nonrecurring.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 OE calculation line by line to the $71.6m cash and $18.0m non-cash charges, separate headquarters costs from other recurring rationalizations, tax-effect only eligible adjustments, and rerun every scenario with a documented normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may overstate cash distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $190.3m of the $209.7m cash balance was held outside the U.S.; removing the entire $209.7m bridge item would reduce value by only $1.71/share
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-distributable operating cash, restrictions and repatriation taxes should reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The repatriation of non-U.S. cash balances from certain subsidiaries could have adverse tax consequences as we may be required to pay and record tax expense on those funds that are repatriated.
audit_findings.explanation: Distributability is unresolved, but the entire cash addition caps the possible bridge overstatement at $209.7m, or 5.6% of base equity value. Even deleting all cash leaves approximately $29.13/share in the base case and $32.52/share in the bull case, still well below the $43.11 market price; therefore it cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document cash by jurisdiction, restrictions, minimum operating requirements and repatriation taxes; replace the bridge amount with verified excess cash, without delaying the conclusion on this item.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped Separation indemnities are outside the OE bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable Separation or tax-indemnity payment would be a claim ahead of common equity and should reduce the equity bridge unless already reflected in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the Separation and Distribution Agreement and certain other agreements with MasterBrand related to the Separation, each party has agreed to indemnify the other for certain liabilities, in each case for uncapped amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: The uncapped contractual exposure is demonstrated, but no outstanding claim, probability or estimable payment is supplied. The record therefore cannot establish materiality. Any liability would reduce value and reinforce the current overvaluation conclusion, but an uncapped exposure could still be important to downside value.
audit_findings.action: Review the Separation and Tax Allocation Agreements, claim notices, triggering events, insurance and MasterBrand credit support; rerun the bridge with any probable or probability-weighted liability supported by that review.

audit_findings.title: Retained pension obligations may require an equity bridge deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.4m combined 2025 pension and postretirement deficit, equal to $0.27/share and 0.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economic defined-benefit deficit not already captured through forecast contributions or OE should be deducted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company retains the primary benefit obligation until the buy-out conversion is completed.
audit_findings.explanation: The retained obligation and $27.8m pension plus $5.6m postretirement deficits are filed facts. Deducting the full $33.4m would reduce base value from $30.84 to about $30.57 per share and cannot close the $12.27 gap to the $43.11 market price. Buy-out pricing remains uncertain, but the recorded deficit is not material to the current conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded status and buy-out settlement requirements, identify amounts already represented in OE or forecast contributions, and deduct only the remaining economic deficit.

audit_findings.title: Performance-share dilution is measured at target rather than maximum payout
audit_findings.magnitude: 444,435 target PSAs equal 0.363% of the 122.490976m-share denominator; incremental above-target dilution is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSA issuance increases fully diluted shares and reduces value per share without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of performance share awards granted are shown below at the target award amounts:
audit_findings.explanation: Target awards are documented, but the supplied record does not state maximum payout multipliers or expected achievement. The known target pool is small relative to the denominator, yet the incremental dilution cannot be capped from the evidence provided, so a concrete not-material determination is unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every outstanding PSA agreement for maximum multipliers and performance status, calculate expected and maximum incremental shares net of supportable forfeitures, and rerun per-share values with the justified denominator.
